title: Symbiont effectors modulate plant signaling to increase host stress resilience
content:
Abstract
Plant-colonizing mutualistic symbionts confer beneficial effects to their hosts, which often includes increased growth as well as biotic and abiotic stress resilience. How these benefits are activated on a molecular level is mostly unknown. Here, we describe effector candidates of the fungal symbiont Serendipita indica (Si), which modulate plant stress signaling pathways. By analyzing the Si effector interactome, we reveal frequent targeting of stress-related host proteins, which are linked to the identified effector signaling functions. Moreover, functional data indicate that Si effectors modulate abiotic stress response of Arabidopsis, as well as resistance to pathogen infection. Analysis of symbiont effectors might not only uncover previously unreported molecular mechanisms that increase plant fitness but might also be used to identify potential genetic traits for crop improvement under changing climates.
